standard.title: Sampling Methods and Distribution Analysis
standard.description: analyse and report on the distribution of data from primary and secondary sources using random and non-random sampling techniques to select and study samples
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can describe and compare distributions using displays and summary statistics (from AC9M7ST01, AC9M7ST02). Students understand random sampling informally.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students compare random and non-random sampling methods, collect samples, analyse and report on distributions from primary and secondary sources.

nodes.label: Comparing sampling methods
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students compare simple random, systematic, stratified and convenience sampling methods and evaluate the reliability of each.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe simple random and systematic sampling; explain which gives a more representative sample and why.
nodes.typical_width: Compare simple random, systematic, stratified, quota and convenience sampling; evaluate reliability and bias potential for each; select appropriate methods for different contexts.
wider: Investigate primary and secondary data sources relating to reconciliation between First Nations Australians and non-Indigenous Australians — analyse the sampling methods used and evaluate their representativeness.
Explore stratified sampling: demonstrate how stratification improves representativeness when a population has distinct subgroups.

response_modes.reason: Understanding the trade-offs between sampling methods requires encountering each in a different context. Students who only know random sampling cannot make informed decisions about stratification or systematic approaches.

nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to collect a sample using a valid method and comment on how that method affects the distribution — students who cannot distinguish and evaluate sampling methods cannot make these methodological choices or reflect on their effect.
nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Reconciliation data sources and stratified sampling design offer advancing students rich methodological depth — evaluating real-world sampling decisions in sensitive social contexts develops both statistical and ethical reasoning.
success_criteria: Describes at least three different sampling methods.
Explains the reliability advantage of random over convenience sampling.
Selects and justifies an appropriate sampling method for a given context.

nodes.label: Analysing and reporting on sample distributions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students collect or obtain a sample, analyse the distribution, and report findings from primary or secondary sources.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect a sample using a specified method; display the distribution and report key features.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse distributions from both primary and secondary sources; report on shape, centre and spread; comment on sampling method and its effect on findings.
wider: Compare distributions obtained from the same population using different sampling methods — does method affect the observed distribution?
Investigate a secondary data source (e.g. ABS data) and evaluate the sampling methodology used — how does it affect confidence in the findings?

response_modes.reason: Reporting on a sample distribution requires integrating sampling method choice, data collection, display creation, statistical description, and contextual interpretation simultaneously.

success_criteria: Collects or obtains a sample using a valid method.
Analyses and describes the distribution appropriately.
Comments on how the sampling method may have affected the distribution.
